# PR #153 round-2 correctness review

## A. Verdict

**BLOCK** at `baa21add0f94f83c014f1c9a0fe8c20bf0a7af5b`: **F003**, the required reissue audit can fail while the standing grant is still returned.

## B. Scope

Only `a0ec95212431b8c12bbd7c477547a5242c8f78c0..baa21ad`. The prior reviewer F001/F002 closures stand. The prime's acceptance of registration-strength authentication under F88 is not reopened; this finding concerns the mandatory audit condition attached to that acceptance. Independent security/performance verdicts remain separately owned.

The detached worktree is clean and pinned. GitHub and `git ls-remote` agree on this full head; the PR is CLEAN. No product edits, local builds/tests, mutation checks or live probes were run.

## C. F003, P2: do not return an unaudited standing grant

`crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:958-1007` makes `audit_grant_reissue` return `()`. A clock failure returns early; a failed `event_bus.publish` is logged and ignored. `register` then unconditionally extracts the same standing token and returns HTTP 200 (`mod.rs:1139-1170`).

This is not a harmless lack of live subscribers: `EventBus::publish` explicitly propagates durable `spine.append` failures (`crates/daemon/src/events/mod.rs:75-94`). On that failure path there is no `context.grant.reissued` row, but the caller still receives the victim's existing grant. The PR's claim that every handout appends an audit event, and the prime's first acceptance condition, therefore hold only on the happy path.

Return a typed audit result and withhold the standing token when persistence fails. Registration can remain valid without a context grant, matching the existing failed-grant fallback, but it must not hand out the protected token without its required audit. Add a focused failing-spine regression: failed append means no standing token returned; a successful retry produces the one audit event. No new authentication mechanism is requested.

This is a source/dataflow proof, not a locally injected storage failure.

## D. Correct behavior retained

`ReportedContext::grant` selects the standing token and `reissued` flag under the same mutex. An unchanged incarnation returns `(same_token, true)`; first issuance or changed incarnation returns `(new_token, false)`. The HTTP path invokes the audit once only for a native reissue, before response construction.

The event has the returned seat, claimed id, harness, folder, pane, pid/start, claimed session, attempt, binding, proc source and connection origin. It explicitly constructs these fields rather than serializing the grant. No token is passed to the audit helper. The production TCP server attaches `ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>` (`crates/daemon/src/serve.rs:29-57`), so origin is not merely a test-only fixture.

After admission, event persistence is independently owned by the existing event bus; no new cancellation-ownership regression was found in that append.

## E. Regression evidence

`http::native_tests::reissued_grant_is_audited_known_limit_f88` executed and passed. It verifies no event on first issuance, the same standing grant on the second registration, exactly one matching spine event, correct seat/pane/pid and loopback origin, token absence, and successful size publication with that grant.

`reported_context::tests::a_grant_is_per_incarnation_and_only_its_token_passes` also executed. The modified unit assertions cover false/true issuance flags and false on rotation. Neither case exercises a failed audit append; green results do not close F003.

## F. Known-limit and cost boundaries

The PR body includes the Known limit and distinguishes Copilot's forged size, genuine-report overwrite, visible state/digest/FYI effects and cold-wake consequences. Squirrel owns the complete honesty/secret assessment of that accepted limit.

This delta adds one attempted spine append per reissued native grant, not per watchdog round or first issuance. It adds no timer, poll or process-launch site. Genuine starts/recoveries can produce the same event; it is evidence of a reissue, not proof of theft. Ocelot owns the rate/cost verdict.
